newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans new tax laws for business - dep p.m..
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans new tax laws for business - dep p.m..

text.p: Forthcoming legislation will scrap tax breaks for foreign investors, Ukraine's deputy prime minister said late on Tuesday.
"To us local and foreign investors are the same," Viktor Pynzenyk told an American Chamber of Commerce meeting.
Under Ukrainian law, foreign businesses which started up soon after independence in 1991 were granted five tax-free years of operation.

Both foreign and domestic investors have long complained about Ukraine's chaotic tax laws and high tax rates, which they said could mean a legally-registered local business could pay a 110 percent tax on its profits.

"We must create favourable conditions for taxes," said Pynzenyk. The unchecked growth of Ukraine's shadow economy, estimated to account for up to 40 percent of all economic activity, is largely blamed on the current tax system.
Pynzenyk said the main change in the new law, to be presented to parliament at the end of the month, would make taxes applicable to earnings instead of starting capital.
Pynzenyk said effective tax collection remained a serious problem. Other steps to be undertaken included the reform of Ukraine's accounting and payroll systems, he said.
